findings.title: buff-span panic-trace chain unwired end-to-end: runtime::init() and .buffmap emission have zero callers
findings.description: The advertised buff-span panic-trace chain (T1/T24, README v1.13 'shipped') is never wired. buff_lang_runtime::init() â€” documented as 'called from generated fn main() startup by the Buff CLI' â€” has zero callers; codegen emits no init call. generate_rust_with_source_map (codegen lib.rs, documented 'The CLI calls this... to emit a .buffmap') also has zero callers and nothing writes .buffmap sidecars. backtrace.rs's hook install is an #[allow(dead_code)] scope-keeper. Generated binaries panic with raw Rust traces; buff backtrace always degrades to its no-sidecar warning.
findings.root_cause: T24 API surface (runtime init fn, codegen source-map wrapper, panic hook, backtrace tool) was built and unit-tested per-piece, but the composition-root call sites in the CLI pipeline and codegen main-body emission were never added; doc comments assert wiring that does not exist.
findings.impact: Primary runtime diagnostic channel silently fails: every `buff run` panic shows generated-.rs line numbers translated onto the .buff filename via an empty SourceMap (commands/run.rs:186-195), actively misleading users; `buff backtrace` can never find a sidecar in real incidents; shipped-feature claim is false.
findings.recommendation: Compose the chain: call generate_rust_with_source_map in build/run, serialize the SourceMap to <exe>.buffmap, plumb the real map into translate_panic, and emit a panic-hook init in generated main() (inline stub for single-file rustc builds where buff-lang-runtime is not linked).
fix_guide: In build/run pipeline, switch to generate_rust_with_source_map and write serialize_to_string output next to the exe as <exe>.buffmap
Pass the real SourceMap into error_mapper::translate_panic in commands/run.rs instead of SourceMap::new()
Emit a panic-hook init statement in generated fn main() when buff-lang-runtime is already an extern crate; otherwise inline a small hook stub so single-file rustc builds still remap
Add an integration test: a panicking program through buff run produces a Buff-mapped trace and buff backtrace locates the sidecar

effort_estimate.breakdown: sidecar write 60 + SourceMap plumbing 60 + hook-emission design/impl 60 + tests 60

findings.technology: Rust workspace (buff-lang-cli, buff-lang-pipeline, buff-lang-codegen-rust, buff-lang-runtime, buff-lang-debug-info)

detection_method.tool: Grep + PowerShell Select-String workspace-wide caller analysis

confidence.rationale: Exhaustive workspace grep shows zero callers for both documented entry points and no .buffmap writers; backtrace install is explicitly dead code; runtime doc comment makes a false claim about CLI behavior.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Both doc comments assert the wiring EXISTS rather than deferring it, so the FP rule (documented deliberate choices) does not apply; verified by exhaustive caller grep plus reading all cited code.

findings.title: Registry has zero request/error logging; tower-http declared for 'tracing middleware' but never used
findings.description: buff-registry ships zero runtime observability: app() installs only DefaultBodyLimit + IP rate limiting â€” no tower-http TraceLayer or any request logging â€” while Cargo.toml declares tower-http specifically to 'add CORS + tracing middleware', which src never references (dead dep, stale comment). A 500 (storage failure), 401, or 429 leaves no server-side evidence beyond three startup eprintlns in main.rs; operators cannot diagnose failed publishes, OAuth callback failures, or abuse from server logs.
findings.root_cause: T57 security hardening added body limits, IP rate limiting, and OAuth, but the tower-http dependency was declared without adopting its trace/cors layers; no logging middleware or handler-level logging was ever added, and no doc defers it.
findings.impact: Server-side blind spot: publishes that fail validation/auth/rate-limit/storage leave no trace; production incidents and abuse are undiscoverable; the Cargo.toml comment misleads maintainers into believing tracing middleware exists.
findings.recommendation: Either enable the tower-http trace feature and add TraceLayer::new_for_http() to app(), or remove the dead dependency and correct the comment; add ERROR-level logging in storage-failure and OAuth-callback paths.
fix_guide: Enable the tower-http "trace" feature in root [workspace.dependencies] and add TraceLayer::new_for_http() in app()
Or remove the unused tower-http dep from crates/buff-registry/Cargo.toml and fix the stale comment
Add error-level logging (eprintln or tracing) in handlers.rs storage-failure and oauth.rs callback-failure arms
Extend tests/registry_tests.rs to assert failing publishes surface a server-side log line

effort_estimate.breakdown: TraceLayer wiring 15 + dep cleanup/comment fix 15 + handler logging/tests 15

detection_method.tool: Grep for tower_http/TraceLayer/tracing across buff-registry src vs Cargo.toml dependency list

confidence.rationale: Mechanically verified: zero tower_http references in src while Cargo.toml:23-30 claims it adds CORS + tracing middleware; app() layers read in full.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: The registry AGENTS.md DEFERRED list omits request logging, so silence is not a documented choice; the stale dependency comment actively contradicts the code.

findings.title: ui dev server terminal-blind: rebuild failures and 404s reach only the browser
findings.description: The ui_dev rebuild loop reports build failures ONLY to the browser via broadcaster.error() â€” the terminal prints nothing after the three startup lines. Cargo/wasm-bindgen stderr is captured into BuildOutcome::Failed::message (builder.rs) and Buff front-end errors are collected (mod.rs) but never echoed to stderr. Users without an open browser tab see nothing; static_handler 404s are silent too. Watch-mode debugging ('why did it stop reloading?') requires attaching a browser.
findings.root_cause: T131 dev server was built broadcast-first: every failure path funnels into ReloadBroadcaster error frames; no stderr mirror was added to rebuild_loop, the builder, or http.rs handlers.
findings.impact: Developers iterating on .buffhtml apps lose the standard Vite-style terminal feedback loop: cargo/wasm-bindgen failures, front-end compile errors, and missing assets are invisible unless a browser tab happens to be connected and rendering the red banner.
findings.recommendation: Mirror every rebuild outcome (ok/failed/error) to stderr with the existing [buff ui dev] prefix; optionally log WS connects and 404 paths at debug level in http.rs.
fix_guide: Echo front-end compile errors (mod.rs errors vector) to stderr before broadcasting
Echo BuildOutcome::Failed messages and builder Err to stderr in rebuild_loop
Add optional request logging (404s, WS connect/disconnect) in ui_dev/http.rs
Add a rebuild_loop test asserting stderr output on failure

effort_estimate.breakdown: stderr mirrors 15 + optional http logging 10 + tests 5

findings.technology: Rust, tokio, axum, notify (buff-lang-cli ui_dev module)

detection_method.tool: Grep of ui_dev sources for terminal writers

confidence.rationale: rebuild_loop (lines 148-184) read in full: the only outputs are broadcaster calls; builder.rs captures cargo/wasm-bindgen stderr exclusively into the browser message; startup/shutdown are the sole eprintlns.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Module docs describe browser broadcast as the outcome channel but never state terminal silence is deliberate; no convention forbids stderr mirrors; dev-server peers (Vite/trunk) log to terminal, so the gap has real debugging cost.

findings.title: No timing or --verbose surface on buff build/run/check
findings.description: buff build / run / check print no timing or phase information and accept no --verbose flag (the cli.rs Build variant has none; build.rs contains zero Instant/elapsed calls). Despite compile speed being a headline feature (v1.25+ bench-compile, --fast linker work), slow-build reports cannot be reproduced with attribution: users get only 'Built <path> (<mode>)' with no duration and no per-phase (lex/parse/codegen/rustc) breakdown outside synthetic bench-compile fixtures.
findings.root_cause: Timing instrumentation was confined to dedicated benchmark subcommands (bench-compile, bench-cold-start, bench-program, bench_harness); the primary user commands never received Instant/elapsed output or a verbose flag.
findings.impact: Users reporting slow compiles (a core selling point of the language) cannot self-serve attribution; maintainers cannot reproduce phase costs on real projects â€” only on synthetic BenchTier fixtures â€” raising triage cost for every compile-speed regression report.
findings.recommendation: Wrap compile+rustc in build.rs with Instant::now() and append elapsed seconds to the Built line; add an opt-in --verbose flag on Build/Run/Check in cli.rs that prints per-phase durations.
fix_guide: Time the compile+rustc span in commands/build.rs (single-file and cargo paths) and append seconds to the Built eprintln
Add #[arg(long)] verbose to Build/Run/Check variants in cli.rs and thread through main.rs dispatch
Print per-phase durations (lex/parse/codegen/rustc) only under --verbose to keep default output clean
Document the flag in --help and the Book build chapter

detection_method.tool: Grep for verbose/Instant/elapsed across cli.rs and command modules

confidence.rationale: Absence verified mechanically (no Instant/elapsed/verbose matches in build.rs/cli.rs Build path), but as an absence-of-feature finding it carries moderate classification subjectivity; bench subcommands partially compensate.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Could be classified as scope rather than defect; however the audit brief explicitly targets compile-diagnostics observability and compile speed is the project's advertised moat, so the missing timing/verbose surface has real debugging cost and no doc declares it deliberately excluded.
